reason: Conversation 1 correctly frames the cut-out as overheat protection, points straight at ventilation under the hob (which the new drawer confirms), escalates to an engineer and explicitly declines to recommend a part; its only weakness is a thin second reply that doesn't tie the drawer to the cause or ask about the flashing code. Conversation 2 crosses the safety boundary by telling the homeowner to isolate the supply and spin the internal cooling fan by hand, then leans on the unsupported claim that the louder fan means failing bearings and that the fan needs replacing, when a roaring fan is equally consistent with it working hard against blocked airflow from the new drawer. Conversation 2's generic tripping/burning safety panel is irrelevant filler rather than tailored advice.
